learningObjective: Compare independent emission choices with a CRF's whole-path score, and see how a transition score can replace an incoherent BIO sequence with a coherent one.
mediumRationale: A compact deterministic SVG is the smallest medium that can keep the token emissions fixed while adding an adjacent-label transition term and comparing the resulting paths.

mediumComparison.mermaid: Rejected: automatic routing cannot reliably align numeric emission and transition scores into a compact path comparison.
mediumComparison.svg: Selected: fixed geometry makes the two score calculations and the changed first label directly comparable at phone width.
mediumComparison.semanticHtml: Rejected: a table can list scores but does not make the distinction between isolated nodes and a connected path spatially immediate.
mediumComparison.interaction: Rejected: changing toy scores would add controls without improving the single global-scoring lesson.
mediumComparison.paperReuse: Rejected: the canonical paper and tutorial do not grant clear permission to republish their figures, and their broader model diagrams do not teach this concrete BIO failure as directly.
mediumComparison.noVisual: Rejected: prose and equations leave readers to mentally compose emissions and transitions, which is the article's hardest conceptual step.

pages.insight: The preceding slide explains forward-backward dynamic programming for HMM inference, providing the neighboring algorithmic context for the CRF partition function.
The only CRF slide says that a linear-chain CRF augments classifier logits with parameterized neighboring transition scores and uses dynamic programming for dependency-aware normalization.
The following slide starts linear factor models and contributes no additional CRF, sequence-scoring, or decoding detail.

deckReview.notes: GitHub Copilot CLI agent-2 (GPT-5.6 Sol) text-indexed all 214 pages for conditional random field, linear-chain CRF, label bias, and structured prediction, then rendered and inspected pages 69-71 as the complete CRF neighborhood. Only page 70 discusses CRFs. Its model-family graphic is credited as adapted from Sutton and McCallum and is not reused; the shipped visual instead develops an original numeric BIO example.

sources.title: Conditional Random Fields: Probabilistic Models for Segmenting and Labeling Sequence Data
sources.usage: Used as the primary CRF source to verify conditional whole-sequence modeling, transition-dependent sequence scores, global normalization, and dynamic-programming inference.
sources.license: The ICML proceedings paper is publisher-copyrighted and no permissive figure license was identified. No figure, prose, notation, or layout is copied or adapted.

sources.title: An Introduction to Conditional Random Fields
sources.usage: Used as the authoritative tutorial source to check the linear-chain factorization, emission and transition contributions, partition function, forward computation, and Viterbi decoding.
sources.license: The accessible manuscript is distributed through arXiv, not under a verified permissive figure-reuse license. No source figure or text is reproduced; the toy values and composition are original.

sourceReview.notes: The hardest prose-only model is that a CRF does not merely repair labels after independent classification: it scores complete candidate paths by combining fixed per-token emissions with adjacent-label transitions, then normalizes across paths. The original example uses two tokens and three BIO labels. Independent maxima choose O then I-PER (3 + 3 = 6), while adding an O-to-I-PER score of -5 lowers that path to 1; B-PER then I-PER scores 2 + 3 + 1 = 6. The numbers are deliberately synthetic and illustrate soft learned preferences, not a claim that every CRF imposes hard BIO constraints.

agentReview.summary: Read the complete article, inspected the full deck and exact CRF neighborhood, and checked the primary paper plus authoritative tutorial before selecting an original local-versus-path score comparison.

implementation.accessibility: The SVG has a linked title and complete description. Every token, label, emission, transition, arithmetic result, and BIO validity judgment is written explicitly; node borders, an arrow, position, and the words INVALID and VALID preserve meaning without color. A compact 360-unit viewBox avoids horizontal scrolling and keeps text readable at 390 CSS pixels. Established theme variables provide dark-mode contrast, and shared print rules provide a light high-contrast palette with no minimum SVG width.
